Convert bulk RNA-seq FPKM to TPM

Source: R/12d-FPKMToTPM.R
FPKMToTPM.Rd

Converts a gene-level FPKM matrix to TPM (Transcripts Per Million). Because the per-gene length factor is constant within a sample, the FPKM-to-TPM transformation requires no gene lengths: each column is scaled so that its values sum to \(10^6\).

For a given sample, every FPKM value is multiplied by \(10^6 / \sum(\text{FPKM})\). Samples whose FPKM column sums to zero produce a zero column in the result and trigger a warning.

Missing values (NA) are either replaced by zero (na_as_zero = TRUE, the default) or trigger an error (na_as_zero = FALSE).

Usage

FPKMToTPM(data, na_as_zero = TRUE, verbose = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

data

A two-dimensional matrix-like object of FPKM values (a base matrix, a data frame, or an S4 Matrix). Rows are genes, columns are samples. Data frames are coerced and must contain only numeric columns. Values must be non-negative and finite.

na_as_zero

A logical flag. If TRUE (default), missing values are replaced by zero before normalization. If FALSE, an error is raised when data contains missing values.

verbose

A logical flag. If TRUE (default), diagnostic messages (missing-value report and completion summary) are shown.

...

Additional arguments passed to CheckNA() when data contains missing values and verbose is TRUE (for example max_print).

Value

A numeric TPM matrix with the same dimensions and dimnames as data. Each column sums to \(10^6\) unless the corresponding FPKM column sums to zero.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Create an FPKM matrix (3 genes x 2 samples)
fpkm <- matrix(
  c(10, 20, 30, 15, 25, 35),
  nrow = 3, ncol = 2,
  dimnames = list(c("GENE1", "GENE2", "GENE3"), c("Sample1", "Sample2"))
)

# Convert FPKM to TPM
tpm <- FPKMToTPM(fpkm)
colSums(tpm)  # Each column should sum to 1e6

# Error if missing values are present and na_as_zero = FALSE
fpkm_na <- fpkm
fpkm_na[1, 1] <- NA
tpm2 <- FPKMToTPM(fpkm_na, na_as_zero = FALSE)
} # }
